note.note:
Action Plan:
1) New-onset left occipital headache:
   - Start an alternative NSAID instead of ibuprofen; take regularly with food. Medication name/dose/route/frequency not documented (e-prescribed to pharmacy).
   - May take acetaminophen (paracetamol) concurrently as needed for pain. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
   - Supportive care: rest and maintain good hydration.
   - Safety-net: seek medical care urgently if pain worsens or if new symptoms develop (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, visual changes, focal weakness/numbness, confusion, or severe sudden “worst headache”).
   - Follow-up: if not settling in 24–48 hours after starting medication, or if recurrent similar episodes occur, contact the clinic for reassessment.
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
- Chief complaint: New headache since yesterday.
- HPI:
  - Onset/duration: Began yesterday mid-morning; built up over a short period; persistent.
  - Location/quality/severity: Left posterior (occipital) region; throbbing; 8/10 intensity.
  - Associated symptoms: Denies nausea, vomiting, photophobia, phonophobia, blurred vision, eye pain, aura, tingling, numbness, weakness, fever, chills, sweats, rash, neck stiffness.
  - Triggers/modifiers: No change with lying down, standing, bending, coughing/sneezing; not time-of-day related. Slept through the night. Normal eating/drinking.
  - Medications tried: Ibuprofen (Nurofen) yesterday; no relief.
  - Impact: Has not missed work but finding work/normal activities difficult.
- Past medical history: None reported. Denies asthma and stomach problems.
- Family history: Mother with hypertension and migraines.
- Medications: None regularly. Ibuprofen yesterday only.
- Social history: Lives with partner; works as a designer; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol; denies recreational drugs.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- Vitals: Not recorded (teleconsultation).
- Examination: Not performed/documented (teleconsultation).
- Investigations: None.

Assessment & Plan:
1. New-onset unilateral occipital headache:
   - Assessment / likely diagnosis: Probable migraine without aura (first episode). Supported by DDx (Medium likelihood) given unilateral throbbing, moderate–severe intensity, gradual onset, maternal history of migraine; lacks full ICHD-3 associated features.
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with DDx):
     • Tension-type headache (Medium): Supported by lack of migrainous accompaniments; less typical due to unilateral throbbing and higher intensity.  
     • Cervicogenic headache (Low–Medium): Unilateral occipital location supports; absence of neck pain/posture triggers opposes.  
     • Occipital neuralgia (Low): Distribution fits; character not typical (not stabbing/paroxysmal).  
     • Cervical (vertebral) artery dissection (Low): Serious cause considered due to unilateral posterior pain; unlikely given gradual onset, no neck pain, no neurologic deficits, no trauma.
   - Investigations planned: None today.
   - Treatment planned:
     • Start alternative NSAID instead of ibuprofen; take regularly with food (name/dose/route/frequency not documented; pharmacy prescription provided).  
     • May take acetaminophen (paracetamol) concurrently (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
     • Rest and maintain hydration.  
     • Safety-net: seek urgent care if worsening headache or new red flags (fever, rash, vomiting, neck stiffness, visual changes, focal neurologic symptoms, sudden severe worst headache).  
     • Follow-up: If not improving in 24–48 hours after starting medication, or if recurrent similar episodes occur, contact clinic for reassessment.
   - Referrals: None at this time.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Medication names/doses/routes/frequencies not documented; allergies not explicitly confirmed; vital signs and neurological exam not performed; blood pressure not measured; pregnancy/LMP and hormonal contraceptive use not assessed; recent caffeine use/changes and potential carbon monoxide exposure not assessed.
- Transcript vs DDx conflicts: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Clear; minor pauses; clinically adequate history documented.
